titulo: GSAP, D3, Three.js, or Lottie: which library for each piece
lead: Each type of motion has one library that solves it in a few lines and another that fights you. Text choreography is GSAP; a chart that comes from data is D3 drawing and GSAP animating; a 3D scene is Three.js; a ready-made After Effects animation is Lottie. In this lesson you choose by asking the right question, and you render a chart and a 3D scene.
objetivo: choose the right library for each piece and render a data chart with D3 and GSAP.

aprende.t: The question that picks the library: what kind of motion is it?
D3 calculates the shape once; GSAP animates it over time
Three.js in HyperFrames: hf-seek and a required data-duration
The error the lint catches when the duration is missing

hero_alt: Four small screens side by side on an editing desk, with a bar chart, a 3D shape, a line icon, and a title.

secoes.titulo: What kind of motion is it?
secoes.sub: Click each option. Several can live together in the same composition.

nos.detalhe: HyperFrames default: text that enters, elements in order, a fixed sequence. Timeline, curves, and stagger. If you are still unsure, start here.
Scales and axes: turns numbers into positions and sizes. In video, D3 draws the SVG once and GSAP animates the bars. D3 alone with its own transitions does not follow the engine's time.
A product spinning, a camera passing through a scene. In HyperFrames, it draws from the hf-seek event and requires data-duration on the root. Covered in depth in course 5 (cinematic sites).
Animation that already has its own timeline (exported from After Effects): an icon, a character that walks. HyperFrames has an adapter for it.
Glow, pulse, a repeating motif, no JavaScript. It needs a finite duration on the root.

secoes.legenda: Map based on the adapters documented in the HyperFrames skills (GSAP, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS, WAAPI, TypeGPU) as of October 19, 2026.

secoes.titulo: Data with D3, motion with GSAP
secoes.sub: Four bars with sample data. D3 computes the scale and position; the timeline makes the bars grow in sequence.

blocos.rot: Terminal · check, render, and run the checker
blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/formacao-cinema-ia-motion-v72/kit
export HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1 NO_COLOR=1
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-motion/a6; rm -rf "$E"; mkdir -p "$E"
cp -r "$K/exemplos/a6-dados" "$E/dados"; cd "$E/dados"
npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 check 2>&1 | grep -E "Check passed|✗"
npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 render --quality draft --workers 2 --quiet --output dados.mp4 > render.log 2>&1
echo "render: $?"
python3 "$K/conferir.py" dados.mp4 6 1920x1080; echo "saída: $?"

abas.html:
◇  Check passed
render: 0
OK: 6,0 s · 1920×1080 · 30 fps · sem áudio
saída: 0

Both libraries come from the CDN with a pinned version (gsap@3.14.2, d3@7.9.0): the render fetches them when the page opens, before the first frame.

Computing a position with getBoundingClientRect inside the animation gives different values depending on which frame is requested, because the engine renders in parallel. Compute everything once, at setup, as the example does with the D3 scales.

secoes.titulo: Three.js tied to the engine's time
secoes.sub: A spinning shape. The rotation comes from the time of the hf-seek event, never from the clock. The trial removes the duration from the root to show the error, then renders the correct version.

blocos.rot: Terminal · lint without and with duration, render and check
blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/formacao-cinema-ia-motion-v72/kit
export HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1 NO_COLOR=1
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-motion/a6; mkdir -p "$E"
rm -rf "$E/three"; cp -r "$K/exemplos/a6-three" "$E/three"; cd "$E/three"
sed -i 's/ data-duration="4"//' index.html   # the common mistake: root without a duration
echo "## sem data-duration"; npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 lint 2>&1 | grep -oE "root_composition_missing_duration_source|[0-9]+ errors?.*"
cp "$K/exemplos/a6-three/index.html" index.html
echo "## com data-duration"; npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 lint 2>&1 | grep -oE "root_composition_missing_duration_source|[0-9]+ errors?.*"
npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 render --quality draft --workers 1 --quiet --output three.mp4 > render.log 2>&1
python3 "$K/conferir.py" three.mp4 4 1920x1080; echo "saída: $?"

abas.html:
## sem data-duration
root_composition_missing_duration_source
1 error(s), 0 warning(s)
## com data-duration
0 errors, 0 warnings
OK: 4,0 s · 1920×1080 · 30 fps · sem áudio
saída: 0

Without GSAP, the root takes data-no-timeline: in 0.8.176 the lint asks for registration in window.__timelines and accepts this attribute as "I don't have a timeline" (found in the lint code on 10/19/2026). The skill's documentation mentions the attribute for a still composition; here the scene moves through hf-seek, not through a timeline.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after you answer.

perguntas.p: A sales-by-month chart, with bars growing one after another. Which combination?
opcoes: Three.js for the bars and CSS for the title text.
A Lottie exported from After Effects with the numbers.
D3 computes the bars and GSAP animates them.
CSS only, with a different animation-delay on each bar.
perguntas.explica: D3 turns data into shape (scale, axis); GSAP handles the order in time, following the engine's clock. CSS can animate too, but you'd do the scale by hand.

perguntas.p: Why does the Three.js composition need data-duration on the root?
opcoes: The adapter can't work out the scene's duration on its own.
Because Three.js can only render at 60 fps.
Because without the duration the 3D scene comes out with no light at all.
Because the lint requires a duration on every composition.
perguntas.explica: With GSAP the engine can infer the duration from the timeline; with Three.js there is nothing to measure. The lint flags it with root_composition_missing_duration_source.

perguntas.p: Where does the 3D scene get the angle for each frame?
opcoes: From Date.now() divided by a thousand on every frame.
From a counter that adds one on every frame drawn.
From the time of the hf-seek event.
perguntas.explica: The engine asks for frames out of order and in parallel; only the time it sends is reliable. A counter and a clock break the determinism from lesson 1.

itens.texto: Choreography, data, 3D, ready-made animation, or repetition: the type picks the library.
D3 calculates once, GSAP animates; Three.js draws through hf-seek.
Without a GSAP timeline, the root needs data-duration.
